title: Web: account switcher shows two accounts active and can't switch
description: Token lives in shared localStorage; with two tabs on different accounts, READY/USER_UPDATE in one tab write its account with the other tab's token (rememberAccount(user, getToken()) and setAuth re-setting the token). Both saved entries end up with the same token: both show the check, switching does nothing. REST calls in the other tab also go out as the wrong account.

title: End-to-end encrypted voice and video calls
description: Per-channel e2ee switch (voice/stage/studio: Manage Channels; DM/group: any member). Per-sender AES-GCM frame keys exchanged pairwise via P-256 ECDH+HKDF over the voice signal relay; mesh uses an encoded-transform worker, LiveKit uses its E2EE with per-participant keys. Safety code from all public keys. Server refuses voice_join without e2ee capability and evicts incapable clients when switched on; clients rejoin on change. Note: voice states are per backend instance, so eviction only covers the instance that handled the PATCH.

title: Phones: message action bar stays open and stacks
description: Tapping a message opened its action bar but nothing closed it; tapping another message opened a second one. Now one shared selection in the store, closed by a tap anywhere outside the message.

title: Android app: Take photo / Record video open the file picker
description: Capacitor's file chooser checks resolveActivity(ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE / ACTION_VIDEO_CAPTURE) before opening the camera. The app targets SDK 36 and its manifest had no <queries> for those intents, so Android 11+ package visibility hid the camera app and Capacitor fell back to the file picker. Fix: declare both intents in <queries> (plus an explicit external-files-path for captured photos). Needs a new APK.

title: MCP integration: Parley as a remote MCP server
description: AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor...) connect at https://<server>/mcp with OAuth 2.1 per the MCP auth spec (RFC 9728/8414/7591/8707, PKCE S256, rotating refresh tokens) and a consent page with four permissions (read, notifications, send, manage). 31 tools wrapping the REST API in-process; MCP tokens limited to an allowlist of REST calls; per-token rate limits and an RL_OAUTH bucket; Settings -> Authorized Apps lists and disconnects assistants.

title: Android: attach sheet Camera only records video
description: The phone attach sheet's Camera input used accept=image/*,video/* with capture; Capacitor's WebView file chooser (and some browsers) then opens only the video recorder, so Android users could not take photos. Split into Take photo (image/*) and Record video (video/*).

title: Photos show rotated in chat
description: Chat thumbnails ignored EXIF orientation (phone photos are stored sideways with a tag) and stored width/height were raw, so photos showed sideways in chat while the original opened upright. Apply orientation to thumbnails, swap dimensions for 90° turns, one-off repair of stored photos.

title: Voice messages don't play on iPhones
description: WebM/Opus voice messages (recorded by Chrome/Firefox/Android) don't play in iOS WebKit (Safari and Chrome on iOS); recorder WebM also lacks duration. Attachments ignored Range requests, and iPhone audio/mp4 recordings sniffed as video/mp4 so weren't treated as voice messages. Fix: convert voice messages to AAC .m4a with a minimal ffmpeg (upload + startup backfill), serve byte ranges, trust declared audio type for MP4 recordings.

title: Composer wraps with larger text; phone attach should open native media pickers
description: With larger text the composer's placeholder wraps and the empty box grows to two lines; GIF/sticker/emoji icons crowd phones. Keep the empty box one line and fold GIF/sticker into the emoji picker when narrow. On touch devices make + open a sheet with Photos & videos, Camera, Files (native pickers), Poll and Voice message.

title: Phone: header scrolls away when typing, keyboard opens on channel change
description: On phones the keyboard scrolls the page so the header (DM or channel name) disappears while typing, and opening a channel focuses the composer, which pops the keyboard. Size the app to the visual viewport and cancel the keyboard scroll; only auto-focus the composer on devices with a fine pointer (Reply still focuses).

title: Opt-in user search; exact username still works
description: Non-admins can find anyone by partial name. Add a privacy setting (off by default) that makes you findable by partial search; otherwise only an exact username matches, which is enough to send a friend request. Admins keep full search.

title: Android: top of the app hard to reach or covered by system bars
description: Android users report the top of the app is cut off or under OS overlays. Make every full-screen surface respect the top safe-area inset.

title: Mobile user settings navigation is hard to use
description: On phones the settings sections are a horizontal scroll strip at the top that is hard to navigate. Use a section list that drills into each section with a back button.

title: Direct messages from friends and server members only, by default
description: New and existing users who never chose should only receive DMs from friends and people they share a server with; others go to message requests or are blocked per the existing setting.

title: Keep the mail log across restarts, with retention and manual removal
description: Admin Mail page reads an in-memory outbox that is lost on restart. Store sent mail in the database, keep it for a configurable number of days, and let admins delete entries (one or all) from the Admin Console.

title: Login page shows a passkey error on load in browsers without passkey support
description: The background autofill (conditional mediation) request reported its NotSupportedError in the login error box. Make the autofill attempt silent; give the button a plain message for NotSupportedError.

title: Home-screen web app opens pages in a browser sheet on iPhone
description: No web app manifest or apple-mobile-web-app tags, so iOS guessed the scope from the page the icon was added on (e.g. /channels/...) and showed every page outside it in an in-app browser sheet. Add a manifest (scope /, standalone), Apple tags, PNG icons, and an nginx rule for the manifest type.

title: Passkeys (WebAuthn) sign-in
description: Add passkeys as an additional sign-in method: register/manage in Settings (after password + 2FA re-auth), sign in from the login page (button + autofill), passkey counts as both factors. webauthn-rs on the server with challenge state in Postgres (works across backends), RP from APP_URL. Hidden where the platform lacks WebAuthn. e2e with a virtual authenticator.

title: Channel drag and drop flickers and lands in unexpected places
description: Every row, category and group container was its own drop target; the gaps between rows belonged to the group container (meaning 'append to group'), so the indicator flashed between a row line and a group outline, and drops in a gap sent the channel to the end of the group. Replace with one list-level handler computing a single insertion point; skip saving unchanged orders.

title: Desktop (Windows): HTML drag and drop never reaches the page
description: Tauri's default native file-drop handler intercepts drag and drop in WebView2, so channel/server reordering and dropping files onto the composer do nothing in the Windows desktop app (no drop events; no PATCH /channels/positions in logs from ParleyDesktop/0.2.1). Disable it on the main window.

title: Channel drag and drop drops twice and can't place after a channel
description: Row drops bubbled to the group container, which re-saved the order with the channel appended to the group (two PATCHes per drop, last one wins). Drops could only go before a channel, so moving down by one did nothing; categories could not be placed after another. Use top/bottom halves with an overlay drop line, stop propagation at rows.

title: Hi-fi calls play stereo as mono
description: Mesh calls rewrote Opus params (stereo=1) only in the SDP sent to peers; the local description kept the default, and libwebrtc configures the receiving decoder from it, so stereo was decoded as mono. Apply the tuned SDP locally too.

title: Studio: muting does not silence your recorded track

Bans, kicks, timeouts and reports work on federated identities (origin_instance+remote_id) so a banned remote user cannot rejoin by recreating a shadow row. Audit log records remote identities.
acceptance_criteria: Denied instance's assertions are rejected; banned remote user is blocked on re-auth; admin UI shows remote users with their origin.

title: Cross-instance guild invites
description: Invite links carry the host instance URL; accepting from a client signed in elsewhere triggers federated login against the host, creates the shadow user and adds membership. Guild/instance settings control whether remote users may join.
acceptance_criteria: Invite created on Y is accepted by a user from X end-to-end (e2e test with two backend instances in docker-compose).

title: Schema: shadow users for remote identities
description: Migration: add users.origin_instance + remote_id (unique together), make email/password_hash nullable for remote rows, scope username uniqueness to local users and render remote names as name@host. Block password/email/MFA/account-export flows for shadow users. All existing FKs keep pointing at users(id).
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies cleanly on existing data; shadow user can join guilds, post, react and be referenced everywhere a local user can; local-only account routes return a clear error for shadow users.

title: Federated login: home instance issues signed identity assertions
description: Home instance endpoint issues a short-lived Ed25519-signed assertion (sub=user id, iss=home URL, aud=target instance, profile snapshot). Target instance verifies it against the issuer's discovery keys and returns its own local session token for that federated identity. Replay protection via nonce/jti and short expiry.
acceptance_criteria: Remote user obtains a session on host instance without a local password; forged, expired, replayed or wrong-audience assertions are rejected; covered by backend tests.

title: Instance identity keys + discovery document
description: Each instance gets an Ed25519 signing keypair (generated on first boot, rotatable) and publishes /.well-known/parley (instance id, canonical URL, public keys, protocol version, federation enabled flag).
acceptance_criteria: Peer can fetch and cache another instance's public key; key rotation keeps the previous key valid for a grace period.

title: Multi-instance client: sign in to and switch between several instances
description: Frontend/desktop/mobile currently hold one instance and API base in store.ts. Refactor to keyed per-instance connections (API base, token, WS, instance settings, guild list) and a unified server sidebar. Useful standalone, and the prerequisite for federated guilds.
acceptance_criteria: Client can be logged in to two instances at once, guilds from both appear in the sidebar, events from both stream live, and logging out of one leaves the other intact.

title: Federation: remote users join guilds hosted on another instance
description: Let self-hosted instance owners invite users from other Parley instances into their guilds. Model: home-hosted guild + federated identity (option B). The guild lives only on its host instance (single source of truth); remote users authenticate via their home instance and get a shadow user row on the host. Clients connect directly to the host's API/WS/LiveKit. Full multi-master guild replication (Matrix/ActivityPub style) is explicitly out of scope.
design: Constraints found: ws/bus.rs uses Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (same-DB only, not cross-install); users.email/password_hash NOT NULL, username UNIQUE; ~47 FKs to users(id); JWTs are HS256 with a per-instance secret (not verifiable by peers); voice is per-instance LiveKit; frontend store assumes a single instance/API base. Shadow user rows keep every FK intact. Remote identities displayed as name@host.
acceptance_criteria: A user registered on instance X can accept an invite to a guild hosted on instance Y, chat/voice there from a single client signed in to X, and be moderated (kick/ban) on Y by federated identity. Instance Y can restrict which instances may federate.
